summary: Safety framing for blades is good: the box cutter and utility knife lines keep 'a careful grown-up' in charge, and the corkscrew deliberately uses fizzy grape juice. Many Commons are well observed (rake in the face, dumbbell toe-stubber, pliers that pinch, tape measure snap-back, screwdriver 'flat when you need a cross', flatpack with three screws left over, the screw that was never left over, polo horse getting the medal, leaf blower leaving children without a pile). The batch has the same structural faults as w12, and they are as widespread. (1) Legendaries: 22 use the endurance formula ('for fifty/a hundred years', 'still has its first rivet/spanner/stuffing'), and most others are sports wins or sincere fixes with no punchline. Names are 82 of 98 'The X That Y'. (2) Epics are overwhelmingly crowd scenes ('every X at the Y', 'the whole class/street/gym'). (3) Rares are often the tool doing its job (oil can fixes squeaks, plane smooths, wrench fixes pipes, file smooths, peeler peels, box cutter cuts tape). (4) Several objects run one trait across three or four rarities (hedge-trimmer topiary, amphibian driving into water, whistle calling people back, flare-like mop floods, sledge knocking down walls, washer stopping drips). (5) Requested clusters are near-identical in places: four gym machines share the 'travelled the distance of X without leaving the room' Legendary and two share the clothes-horse Common and New Year rush Epic; fairy lights and string lights duplicate Common (tangle), Uncommon (one bulb out) and Epic (garden party); bolt and nut have the same 'rolled off the bench, whole workshop searched' Epic; nut and washer the same rolls-under-the-cupboard Common; cable and USB cable the same 'which no cable has ever done' Legendary; box cutter and utility knife the same 'never cut what was inside' Legendary; kick pad and punching bag the same 'a million hits and still...' Legendary; axe and saw the same stuck-in-the-wood Common; knot, chain and rope all hold a boat in a storm. The sports sticks (golf club, tee, hurling, lacrosse, croquet, polo) all end on 'won the final / scored the winner'. (6) Cross-batch near-copies: i_slot repeats w10 x_slot_machine (lever every child pulls, pier arcade, same pier for decades), the javelin lands in the long jump pit like w06 discus, the jump rope craze repeats w11 hula hoop, the hose water fight w09 water gun, the ice axe 'now hangs on the hut wall' w10 power bank, the chisel's paint-tin opener the screwdriver Rare, plus smaller echoes (rubber band, toothpick, extension cord, steam cleaner, crochet blanket, cherry picker kitten). Hard flags: i_slot is a one-armed bandit with 'Bandit' names, a 'Jackpot' Ultimate and children pulling the lever; it needs a no-gambling rewrite. 'Hammer Time Boost' is a meme. The envelope opener invites waving it like a sword ('Sword Swing'). The ladder Epic drops paint on the cat. The cable car's 'Rusty Cable' and 'Frayed Cable' moves are frightening for a passenger ride. The ice axe Ultimate 'Glacier Swing' is cold while two variants burn; the amphibian Ultimate is a burn with no heat; the wrench 'Pipe Fix' and treadmill 'Belt Speed Up' sound like buffs on attacks. Clumsy suffixed names are common ('Handle Guard Trowel', 'Sawing Boost Boost', 'Second Coat Boost Boost', 'Rusty Hook Bite Cord', 'Water Bottle Rest Rest', 'Handle Bonk Knife'). Replacements are given for every high and medium item, and new names were checked against all curated files and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Legendary is the 'has done X for N years / still has its first ...' endurance formula.
patterns.suggestion: Rewrite as one outrageous feat with a punchline (oil can: the clock tower gives the town two lunchtimes; toolbox: things start breaking on purpose to get a visit; nail: the wall gives up first).

patterns.pattern: Sports Legendaries all end on 'won the final / scored the winner / framed it' with no joke.
patterns.suggestion: Keep polo (the horse gets the medal is the model). Give the others an absurd consequence instead of a trophy (golf club wins a game on the next course; lacrosse catches a seagull's lunch).

patterns.pattern: Epic is a crowd scene ('every X at the Y', 'the whole class/street/gym at once') with no concrete consequence or joke.
patterns.suggestion: Make something happen with a specific funny result (kick pad stuffing turns the hall into a snow globe; medal ribbons tie the fun-run finishers into a giant necklace).

patterns.pattern: Rare is the tool doing its job well, not a troublesome power.
patterns.suggestion: Give it a power that causes trouble (wrench grips nuts from across the room; plane smooths the cat so it slides off sofas; reel winds in before the fish has decided to bite).

patterns.pattern: One trait carried across three or four rarities.
patterns.suggestion: Let the headline trait own at most two rarities; replacements are in the issues.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name monotony: 82 of 98 are 'The X That Y'; two are 'Old X of the Y'.
patterns.suggestion: Mix shapes ('Name, the Epithet', coined single names, title + name). Per-id names are given where the lore changes; untouched ones can follow the same mix.

patterns.pattern: Monster name describes another rarity or contradicts its own line.
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair per the issues (hook: C 'Snagger', U 'Woollymonster Hook'; file tool: C 'Scrapescreech', U 'Nailfiler'; whistle: U 'Pearattle').

patterns.pattern: Near-identical clusters inside the batch (the requested groups).
patterns.suggestion: Which side changes is named in each issue.

patterns.pattern: Near-copies of earlier drafts (w10 slot machine, w06 discus, w11 hula hoop, w09 water gun, w10 power bank, w11 rubber band, w11 toothpick, w10 extension cord, w09 steam cleaner, w05 cherry picker, w08 buckle, w11 crochet hook).
patterns.suggestion: Change the w13 side (replacements in the issues).

patterns.pattern: i_slot: one-armed bandit framed with gambling glamour (Bandit names, Jackpot, children pulling the lever, millions of children).
patterns.suggestion: Reframe as a retired seaside noise-machine that never pays out; no jackpot, no lever-pulling children (see issues).

patterns.pattern: Clumsy suffixed or doubled move names.
patterns.suggestion: Drop the object word at the end and doubled verbs ('Handle Guard Trowel' -> 'Handle Guard', 'Sawing Boost Boost' -> 'Fresh Blade Boost').

patterns.pattern: Move names untruthful to the mechanics or repeating the Epic name.
patterns.suggestion: Heat words only on burn, no cold words when a variant burns, no heal or buff words on attacks, one-hit moves not tripled, Ultimates with their own image.
